---
title: "OpenSASE"
subtitle: "Self-hosted SASE-style TLS inspection, declared end-to-end with Nix"
---

OpenSASE is an open, self-hosted take on the SASE edge: clients connect over **OpenVPN**, their traffic is **decrypted and re-encrypted by mitmproxy** according to a URL-category policy, every payload is scanned by **ClamAV**, and every verdict — splice, bump, clean, INFECTED — is written to a JSONL decision log you can pipe into anything.

Two ways to run it, from one repo:

::: { layout-ncol="2" }
### Containers — no Nix needed

Pre-built OCI images are published to GHCR by CI. Pull them and `docker compose up` on Linux, macOS, or Windows with any OCI runtime.

[Deploy with Docker →](docs/deployment.qmd)

### NixOS appliance

The same stack as stock NixOS modules: boot it in QEMU, rebuild it on a real machine, or deploy with `nixos-rebuild --target-host`.

[Deploy with Nix →](docs/deployment.qmd)
:::

## Why Nix end-to-end?

- **No floating bases.** Every image and appliance closure is a hash-pinned derivation from the same nixpkgs — what CI builds is byte-identical to what you build.
- **Declare, don't assemble.** The appliance is `services.clamav` + `services.dnsmasq` + `services.openvpn` + a `services.opensase` module, not five hand-written Dockerfiles.
- **Portability for free.** Non-Nix users never touch Nix: they pull the GHCR images `dockerTools` produced.

```{mermaid}
flowchart LR
    client["VPN client"] --> vpn["openvpn udp/5443"]
    vpn --> mitm["mitmproxy<br/>splice | bump per URL category"]
    mitm --> clam["clamd :3310"]
    mitm --> log[("decisions.jsonl")]
    mitm --> net((Internet))
```
